NDT training in Williston: how it works for Williston employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Williston and Bakken employers and technicians. Theory runs live online, and practical training runs onsite at your yard, shop or facility. Level I, II and III courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET under ASNT Level III oversight. Once training, experience and exams are done, your employer certifies you under its own written practice. Nobody in the crew has to make a long winter drive to a distant classroom.

In Williston, distance decides almost everything. The Bakken covers several counties of northwest North Dakota and reaches into eastern Montana. An inspection crew can easily spend more of its day on US-2, US-85 and county gravel than on the job. Sending technicians to a training centre in a large city means days of lost billable time, travel and lodging. For most Bakken employers, the smarter option is live online theory, done from a man-camp room, a home in Williston or Watford City, or the shop's break room, followed by an onsite practical at the employer's own yard.

We are open about how this works. Atlantis has no training centre in Williston, and we do not claim one. What we provide is ASNT Level III-supervised training that fits into your crew's schedule and produces records your written practice can use. If a single individual would honestly be better served by a scheduled course elsewhere, we will say so.

If you already know what you need, request a Williston training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Williston

All courses are built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. For recommended training and experience hours by method and level, see our training-requirements matrix. Your employer's written practice sets the figures that apply to you.

MethodLevelsWhat Williston employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic)I, II, III prepWall thickness on facility piping, separators, heater-treaters and vessels; weld examination on gathering-line and station piping; erosion monitoring at elbows and chokesNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
PAUT (phased array)II, III prepEncoded girth-weld examination on gathering and transmission lines, corrosion mapping at gas plants and compressor stationsUT Level II or UT knowledge accepted by the written practice
TOFDII, III prepHeavy-wall weld sizing on plant piping and pressure vessels, paired with PAUTUT Level II
RT (radiographic)I, II, III prepPipeline girth welds to API 1104 during construction and tie-ins, station piping, vessel repairsNone for Level I; radiographer certification and radiation-safety training required separately
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepPipe at integrity digs, structural welds, drilling and workover equipment, tank shell and nozzle weldsNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepStainless and non-magnetic components, valve bodies, weld root and crater checks, surface checks where MT cannot be usedNone for Level I
VT (visual)I, II, III prepWeld visual during pipeline and facility construction, in-service visual on tanks, vessels and structures, coating and corrosion assessmentNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepHeat-exchanger and cooler tubing at gas-processing plants, crack detection through coatings on weldsNone for Level I

UT. Most Bakken UT work is thickness. It happens on the separators, treaters, flowlines, headers and vessels that sit on every well pad and at every facility, and on the elbows and tees where produced water and sand erode steel. The course covers sound physics, calibration, straight-beam thickness technique with dual-element probes, and angle-beam weld examination. It also covers two North Dakota realities: temperature-corrected measurements and couplant behaviour in cold weather. Level II adds interpretation and reporting against the procedure and code.

PAUT and TOFD. Pipeline construction and replacement work increasingly uses encoded ultrasonic examination in place of film. The advanced-UT courses cover focal laws, encoded scanning, analysis of girth-weld data, and TOFD sizing. For an experienced Bakken UT Level II, this is often the best-value next step.

RT. The course covers gamma and X-ray sources, exposure calculations, film and digital detectors, image quality indicators and weld interpretation to API 1104. Radiography remains central to pipeline construction in the basin. Anyone working in RT must also meet the separate radiation-safety and radiographer-certification requirements described below.

MT and PT. These are the surface methods used at integrity digs, in fabrication shops, on equipment repairs and on tank welds. Cold weather matters here as well. Penetrant procedures have a qualified temperature range (the standard range in ASME Section V is roughly 40 to 125 degrees Fahrenheit), and working outside it requires a procedure qualified for that temperature. MT particle and bath behaviour also changes in the cold. We teach why the limits exist and how procedures deal with them, not just what the numbers are.

VT. Visual testing is the method that sees most Bakken construction welds first. The course covers visual acuity, lighting (short winter days make this a real issue), gauges, and API 1104 and ASME visual acceptance criteria.

ET. The course is for gas-plant and compressor-station technicians who deal with exchanger and cooler tubing. It covers impedance-plane interpretation, probe and frequency selection, and reference standards.

Level III. Experienced Level IIs who want to take on procedure and certification responsibility can prepare through our ASNT Level III programme. ASNT administers the Level III exams directly.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Williston, step by step

  1. Confirm the written practice. Your employer's written practice sets hours, exams, grading and recertification. If you are new to the basin, ask your prospective employer which methods it certifies first. In the Bakken that is usually UT thickness, MT and VT.
  2. Complete formal training. Classroom hours for the method and level, taken live online around rotations or onsite. The training-requirements matrix lists recommended hours.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Supervised experience in the method, documented and signed. On a two-weeks-on rotation the hours build quickly, but only the logged hours count. Keep your log current, including dates, locations, method and supervisor.
  4. General exam. Written exam on the principles of the method, given under a Level III.
  5. Specific exam. Written exam on your employer's procedures, equipment, and the codes you work to (API 1104, ASME B31.3 or B31.4/B31.8, or the operator's specification).
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on exam on specimens with real discontinuities, graded by a Level III.
  7. Vision exam. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast. Near vision is re-checked at least annually.
  8. Employer certification. The employer certifies you in writing, and the records are kept on file for operator audits.
  9. Recertification. Follows the interval in the written practice (SNT-TC-1A recommends a maximum of five years). When you move to another contractor, which is common in the basin, the new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice and may credit your documented history.

Background reading: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Williston crews

The Bakken's working pattern shapes how training should be delivered.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led virtual sessions. Technicians on rotation can take theory during days off or evenings instead of losing a hitch to a classroom. Connectivity is weak across much of the basin, so sessions are best joined from town, a camp with decent internet or the shop. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your yard or facility. Practical training and exams at your Williston, Watford City, Tioga or Dickinson location, using your instruments and specimens cut from the kind of pipe and fittings your crews examine. This is the most efficient model for contractors with several technicians to qualify.
  • Blended. Online theory first, then a concentrated onsite practical block, scheduled between rotations.

Seasons matter as well. Pipeline and facility construction peaks in the warmer months, when crews are hardest to release. Winter slows construction but brings conditions that make outdoor practical sessions hard. Many Bakken employers therefore run theory during slower periods and hold practicals indoors in a heated shop. Plant turnarounds at gas-processing facilities create their own busy windows. We build the calendar around your workload, not ours. For multi-crew programmes, see corporate NDT training.

The practical exam is never done by video. Ask about onsite training for your Williston crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Williston

Well pads, tank batteries and facilities. Thousands of producing wells feed separators, heater-treaters, storage tanks, flares and water-handling equipment. These pressure vessels and piping systems need UT thickness surveys, VT and repair NDT throughout their lives, and produced-water and sand erosion keeps the thickness work steady.

Gathering and midstream. Crude, gas and water gathering systems run across the basin to processing plants, rail terminals and transmission lines. Large gas-processing plants, such as the long-established plant at Tioga and newer ones in McKenzie County, need NDT during construction, expansions and turnarounds. Crude leaves the basin by pipeline, including the Dakota Access Pipeline, and by rail. All of this work runs on API 1104 for pipeline welding, ASME B31.4 and B31.8 for pipelines, ASME B31.3 inside plants, and ASME Section VIII for vessels. Storage tanks are usually built and maintained to API 650 and 653.

Pipeline regulation. Interstate pipelines are regulated by the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration under 49 CFR Parts 192 (gas) and 195 (hazardous liquids). North Dakota's Public Service Commission carries out pipeline safety oversight for intrastate gas systems, and the state's oil and gas regulators oversee production-side operations. For NDT technicians, two requirements go together. You need NDT method certification under your employer's written practice, and for covered pipeline tasks you need Operator Qualification (OQ) under the operator's plan. They are separate, and operators check both.

Fabrication and equipment shops. Williston, Watford City, Tioga and Dickinson have fabrication shops building skids, piping spools, tanks and pressure equipment, plus shops repairing drilling, completion and workover equipment. They use VT, MT, PT and UT, with RT on code welds.

Power and rail. Coal-fired and gas-fired generating stations elsewhere in North Dakota and the rail infrastructure serving the basin add outage and structural NDT work to the regional market.

Radiography licensing in North Dakota. North Dakota is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials used in industrial radiography are licensed and inspected by the North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality radiation control programme, which also registers radiation-producing machines. Radiographers using sources must hold radiographer certification (typically through the ASNT Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel programme or a recognised state programme) and work under the licensee's radiation-safety programme. Crews based in Montana or elsewhere must meet reciprocity requirements before working with sources in North Dakota, and the Montana side of the basin has its own regulatory arrangements. SNT-TC-1A RT certification covers technique and film or digital interpretation. It does not authorise you to use a source.

What Bakken employers ask for. Postings most often ask for SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT (thickness and shear wave), MT and VT, with RT and radiographer certification for pipeline construction and PAUT for advanced roles. Pipeline work also asks for OQ. Some owners ask for API 510, 570 or 653 inspector certifications or CWI. We do not train those schemes. They are arranged through their own bodies. For pay information, see the NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Williston NDT companies

The boom-and-bust rhythm of the Bakken has left many small inspection contractors with capable Level IIs, a fast-changing crew and no full-time Level III. When an operator audits your technicians, it will ask for the written practice, the exam records and the vision records, and it expects them to agree with each other. Atlantis supports these employers directly:

  • Written-practice development. A written practice that fits the methods and levels you actually use and the operator specifications you work to. See NDT written practice development.
  • Outsourced Level III. Exam administration, procedure and technique approval, and certification-file review, including taking over the records of technicians who move between contractors so they can be re-certified cleanly under your written practice.
  • Audit readiness. Before an operator pre-qualification or audit, we check your records against your written practice and highlight any gaps.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance. A plain-language explanation of employer-based certification for owners and operations managers: SNT-TC-1A certification.

Book a Level III consultation and tell us your methods, crew size and the operator requirements you are working to.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator offers 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Bakken technicians, the oil and gas site and storage-tank environments match daily work closely. The simulator can be used during downtime to rehearse set-ups, scan patterns and indication recognition.

The simulator is practice, not qualification. It does not replace hands-on training on real instruments or the practical exam on real specimens that your written practice requires.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, exams and practical assessment. Onsite programmes for Williston employers run under that ASNT Level III oversight.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Williston

How do I get NDT certified in Williston?

Your employer certifies you under its written practice, based on SNT-TC-1A. You complete formal training, log supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and helps employers with written practices and Level III services.

Can I take NDT training online in North Dakota?

Yes, for theory. Live online sessions fit around rotations. Practical training and the practical exam must be done hands-on, usually onsite at your employer's yard or shop. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and on whether you already hold UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours, which are listed in our training-requirements matrix. On a busy rotation, documented experience often builds quickly once you are logging it properly.

Do I need a license for radiography in North Dakota?

North Dakota is an Agreement State, so the state's Department of Environmental Quality licenses radioactive materials used in radiography. Each radiographer must hold radiographer certification and work under the licensee's radiation-safety programme. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is a separate requirement for technique and interpretation.

What does NDT training cost in Williston?

We do not publish prices. The cost depends on method, level, group size and whether training is online, onsite or blended. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Request a Williston training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Bakken employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the normal basis for NDT personnel certification among the contractors and operators working in the basin. Because it is employer-based, each new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice.

Is NDT certification the same as Operator Qualification?

No. OQ is a federal pipeline-safety requirement for covered tasks, administered under the operator's OQ plan. NDT certification shows competence in the inspection method under your employer's written practice. Pipeline work in the Bakken usually needs both.

Can NDT be done in North Dakota winter conditions?

Yes, within procedure limits. Penetrant and some MT techniques have qualified temperature ranges, UT readings need temperature consideration, and equipment and batteries behave differently in extreme cold. Procedures must be qualified for the conditions, and training covers why.

Which method should a new Bakken technician learn first?

UT thickness, MT and VT cover most entry-level work. Add RT with radiographer certification for pipeline construction, then PAUT once you hold UT Level II.

Can you train our crew at our yard?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your facility is our standard model for crews. Ask about onsite training for your Williston crew.

Do you train for API 653 or CWI?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some tank owners and fabricators also ask for API 653 or CWI, which are separate schemes with their own certifying bodies.

How should I prepare for the practical exam?

Rehearse set-ups on the Practical NDT simulator, work through mock questions such as our UT Level 2 practice questions, and get as much supervised time on real equipment as your employer allows.
